spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:** The first who grieves is the Divine Love itself in its maternal proceeding, from which all spiritual life originates. She sorrows on account of the goods and truths that proceed from her, which have been brought into states of temptation — for they were conjoined with falsity from evil and with the destructive perversion that corrupts all good. They have been held captive under the entire dominion of the hells. For what cause did she grieve, keeping watch over them as they endured these temptations? Whenever she might perceive their states, and how spiritual suffering is inflicted upon them, she grieves and is without peace on their account.

**¶3:** The second who is troubled inwardly is the Divine Wisdom in its primal human form, whose sovereignty and dominion are established in the vessel of illuminated doctrine [GAP-1: ...]. And he too is troubled inwardly on account of his five interior perceptions — the faculties of spiritual sensation proceeding from him — which are set in the midst of spiritual peril. For at whatever time he may perceive that they are assailed by temptation, always he hears the interior lamentation of their anguish as they cry out because of the assaults and injuries of the falsity from evil that wars against them continually; and as he perceives them thus without ceasing, he grieves and mourns on account of those perceptions of truth that proceed from him.

---

**A note on method:** The "five sons" of the First Man correspond in Manichaean cosmology to the five light-elements, but read as correspondence these are the five interior faculties of spiritual perception — the capacity by which wisdom apprehends reality — now immersed in states where falsity assails them. The "Mother" and the "First Man" together represent the Divine Love and the Divine Wisdom in their grieving solicitude over all that proceeds from them into the combat of temptation.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The first who grieves is the first Mother of Life. She is sad because of her children who are set in affliction, for they were conjoined with the Darkness and the [poi]son. They have been bound with the entire ruling-power. For what was she grieving, [wa]tching over them taking these afflictions? Whenever she might [s]ee them and how suffering is brought upon them, she shall grieve and be unhappy on account of them.

[The s]econd one who is troubled of heart is the First Man, whose [great]ness and kingdom is established in the li[ght] ship [of the sun]. And he too is troubled of heart because of his five sons who are set in the midst of danger. For any time he may see that they are given trouble, always he might hear the sound of their weeping as they cry out because of the blows and wounds of the enemy who assaults them daily; and as he sees them like this constantly, he shall g[ri]eve and mourn on account of his [s]o[n]s.

fills.explanation: In Manichaean cosmology the Sun is the primary "light ship" where the First Man's sovereignty is established, and in correspondential terms the Sun represents illuminated doctrine — precisely what the spiritual reading indicates at this position.
